overview: This 323-page file brings together Japanese overseas broadcast magazines, shortwave schedules, listener correspondence, U.S. diplomatic reports, and FBI-transmitted broadcast transcripts. Its 1940–1941 materials show how Radio Tokyo promoted Japanese culture and wartime policy to international audiences while U.S. officials tracked its reach and messages.
interest: Regional editions, listener forms, and monitored transcripts let historians compare Japan’s intended audiences with its broadcast messages.
